executionHistory.summary: Authored the MCP Knowledge Server specification: intent, success signal, hard constraints, the D1-D5 decisions, the toolset and refusal vocabularies, the section 15 documentation table, and the section 18 operator review gate. Surfaced findings F-109-001 through F-109-006, including the BUG-019-003 dependency that leaves hospitality-read specified but not deliverable. No source edited, no tests executed, no evidence claimed.

Added spec.md section 9A, the Non-UI UX Contract: the operator and client-developer experience requirements R-109-UX01 through R-109-UX18, the OF-1 through OF-3 operator flows, and the refusal-rendering cases. Raised findings UX-F-001 through UX-F-005 covering the corpus-grant ownership ambiguity, the missing section 17.1 documentation row, the principle-numbering mismatch, the incomplete section 2 Success Signal, and the D1 'fully coded' wording conflict. No source edited, no tests executed, no evidence claimed.

Authored the design: the MCP-owned audience-bound credential and authorizer, the four-gate authorization pipeline, the raw-content-incapable projection type, the refusal vocabulary and Case A indistinguishability rule, the audit ledger, and the memory-write deferral mapping. Section 4 resolves UX-F-001 by making the corpus grant an MCP-owned data-scope Grant kind rather than consuming spec 108's corpus:read, which surfaced the new open finding F-109-OF2-AMEND. No source edited, no tests executed, no evidence claimed.

Converted the spec and design into a seven-scope sequential plan: MCP foundation, context toolset with readiness-filtered discovery, memory-read over the spec-095 executor with projection enforcement, person-context, graph-read with the scope-minimized step-up challenge, hospitality-read as honestly unavailable, and the documentation/release/configuration scope. 43 Test Plan rows each with a matching DoD item, plus 14 standing regression DoD items (two per scope) for 57 test DoD items in total. Scope 06 recorded Blocked on BUG-019-003 rather than planned as deliverable. No source edited under the G073 lockout, no tests executed, no evidence claimed.

RATIFICATION RUN. The operator DELEGATED all seven spec.md section 18 decisions with the standing instruction 'pick the best option for long term, no shortcuts'. Section 18 was converted from an open review gate into a ratified decision record dated 2026-07-29, preserving item numbering 1-7 so every existing cross-reference stays valid. Decisions: (1) D1 accepted, with a NEW binding honesty constraint - the only permitted egress claim is 'Smackerel never sends your knowledge anywhere; a client you explicitly authorize may', and any text implying Smackerel enforces client-side inference locality is a defect; (2) D2 accepted as permanent with no escape hatch, and no future spec may add a raw-content toolset without superseding it; (3) D4 accepted WITH A CARVE-OUT - prompts, Apps, subscriptions and notifications/tools/list_changed are permanently deleted, but OAuth 2.1 + DCR + RFC 9728 are NOT deleted, they are out of scope with the named re-open trigger 'a client outside the operator's control must connect to /mcp', because calling them permanently deleted would have been overclaiming; (4) external toolset accepted permanently off; (5) J4 sequencing accepted, hospitality-read waits for BUG-019-003; (6) spec 095 exposure accepted, with its side benefit and its first-consumer risk both recorded; (7) principle gap RESOLVED BY ADDITION - docs/Product-Principles.md gains Principle 11 'Your Data Stays Yours' and Constitution C1 is not the sole carrier. Consequential edits: spec.md D4 and section 13 amended to carry the item-3 split; section 16's principle-gap note changed from open owner decision to resolved; section 9A.7 re-routed UX-F-002, UX-F-004 and UX-F-005 to bubbles.analyst because the gate closed WITHOUT deciding them - they are spec.md wording corrections, not product decisions, and recording them as ratified would have been overclaiming. scopes.md Scope 07 gained two owner-sign-off DoD items (add Principle 11 to the owner-ratified docs/Product-Principles.md, and add a matching block to its BLOCKING companion enforcement file .github/instructions/product-principles.instructions.md) and TP-07-03 was extended to verify both, with an adversarial case that fails if the principle ships unenforced; a pre-existing fused TP-07-05/TP-07-06 markdown table row was repaired into two rows with content preserved verbatim. OWNERSHIP DEVIATION, recorded rather than hidden: spec.md and design.md are not bubbles.plan-owned artifacts and were edited only under the operator's explicit written instruction to convert section 18 and to correct any artifact still asserting these decisions are open. NO status change (specs_hardened before and after), NO certification field altered, NO phase claim added, NO implementation claimed, NO test executed, NO evidence asserted. docs/Product-Principles.md itself was NOT edited - it is owner-ratified and its amendment is a delivery-time obligation requiring owner sign-off.

GAP-CLOSURE RUN. Two verified gaps closed, additively. GAP 1 - NO MCP TOOL NAMES EXISTED. The packet named toolsets (context, memory-read, graph-read, hospitality-read, person-context, memory-write) but never named the individual tools a client sees in tools/list; the only concrete smackerel_ names in spec.md were the five Prometheus metric families. An MCP tool name is a stable PUBLIC WIRE CONTRACT that clients pin in config, so it must be planned rather than emerge from an implementation. spec.md D5 gained a normative Tool Inventory table (Tool, Toolset, Required grants, readOnly, destructive, idempotent, openWorld, Description) covering nine names: smackerel_active_topics, smackerel_daily_brief, smackerel_server_context, smackerel_get_artifact, smackerel_recall, smackerel_person_context, smackerel_graph_neighbors, smackerel_graph_topic, smackerel_guesthost_context. ADJUSTMENT RECORDED HONESTLY: the request suggested six names; nine are listed because section 8.2 already enumerates eight served logical tools, and naming only six would have left graph.get_topic, context.get_daily_brief and context.get_active_topics as orphans - an internal contradiction inside a hardened spec, which is the exact defect class this run exists to remove. Every row maps to its section 8.2 logical identifier, and section 8.2 gained context.get_server_context so the two tables are two-way consistent. Three normative notes added: T1 name rule (1-128 chars, case-sensitive, unique, A-Za-z0-9_-. only; registration refuses a duplicate, an out-of-charset name, or a name absent from the inventory), T2 ordering contract (the table row order IS the deterministic tools/list order and is exactly design.md section 5's (toolset ordinal, name ascending) sort, so the two are one fact rather than two competing sources; MAY vary by credential per request, MUST NOT vary per-connection), and T3 annotations-are-advisory (the MCP specification requires clients to treat annotations as untrusted, so server-side P-AUTHZ / P-EGRESS / P-PROJ is what enforces). T4 records that memory-write, assistant, operations and external export no names. GAP 2 - MCP RESOURCES WERE NEITHER SPECIFIED NOR EXCLUDED. D4a deletes resource SUBSCRIPTIONS only, so Resources as a read primitive were simply absent - zero occurrences of resource_link, smackerel://, resources/list or a URI template anywhere in the packet. Silence was the defect. New spec.md section 9B records the ratified split. IN SCOPE: resource_link entries in tool results (returning a REFERENCE instead of inlining content directly reinforces D2 - a link is categorically not content_raw and it removes the pressure to inline a body), smackerel_recall returning compact Projections plus resource_link entries, and exactly five URI templates - smackerel://artifact/{id}, smackerel://topic/{id}, smackerel://person/{id}, smackerel://place/{id}, smackerel://guesthost/{kind}/{opaque-id}. BINDING R-109-RES3: no PII in a resource URI - no guest email, no person name, no raw external identifier - because a URI is an egress surface in its own right (logged by intermediaries, rendered in client UIs, retained where the body is not), so a PII-bearing URI would make D2 true of the payload and false of the envelope. EXCLUDED and added to section 13: no enumerable resources/list over the corpus and no whole-graph resource, because an enumerable list is a CORPUS-ENUMERATION ORACLE that leaks existence and volume even when every individual read is denied, contradicting the bare-403 / no-existence-oracle denial doctrine R-109-UX12 and F-109-006 enforce everywhere else. Resources are addressable by template, never browsable. design.md records where names are registered (internal/mcp/capability, Descriptor.ID as a literal on the manifest slice, validated at registration against the D5 inventory, never derived from agent.All() or a map key) and where resource_link is emitted (internal/mcp/projection owns the single ResourceURI(kind, id) constructor whose id is an OpaqueID newtype - so a name or email address is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a review finding, the same structural stance mechanism 1 takes for content_raw - with transport appending links beside the typed []projection.Artifact and registering no resources/list). Consistency preserved with P-PROJ and section 7 mechanisms 1-3: a resource_link is a sibling transport content entry, never a Projection field, so section 9's closed field set is untouched. scopes.md gained SCN-109-P04 with TP-02-07 (unit, two-way set equality against the D5 inventory plus the T1 name rule plus inventory-order serving; adversarial against registering a well-formed name absent from the inventory) and SCN-109-P05 with TP-03-10 (integration, seeded person name and email markers scanned across every emitted URI; adversarial against a human-readable title slug, which passes a payload-only content_raw scan and fails only this one because the leak is in the envelope). Test Plan rows 43 to 45 with matching DoD items; test DoD items 57 to 59; Scope 02 6 to 7 rows, Scope 03 9 to 10 rows. scenario-manifest.json kept at EXACT SCN-109-* parity with scopes.md. OWNERSHIP DEVIATION, recorded rather than hidden: spec.md and design.md are not bubbles.plan-owned artifacts and were edited only under the operator's explicit written instruction to close these two gaps in this directory.
